questions.q: Strip away the UI — what is a dbt Cloud job, according to this lesson?
options: An ordered list of commands to run, plus something that decides when to run them
A single dbt model with no commands attached
A GitHub Actions workflow file stored inside dbt Cloud
A warehouse object created automatically by dbt
questions.explain: A job is just an ordered command list (Execute Steps) plus a trigger condition — schedule, PR, or API.

questions.q: The lesson says last lesson's CI check was actually which kind of job?
options: The same job infrastructure, just with the trigger set to "on pull request" instead of a schedule
A completely separate system unrelated to jobs
Something only possible outside of dbt Cloud
A job that can only ever run once and never again
questions.explain: CI jobs and scheduled jobs are the same underlying feature — they just differ in trigger condition.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three trigger types this lesson describes for a dbt Cloud job?
options: Triggered automatically whenever any employee logs into Slack
Scheduled via a cron expression
On pull request
Via an external API call
questions.explain: The three trigger types are: scheduled (cron), on pull request, and API-triggered. Slack logins aren't a dbt Cloud job trigger.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when might a team prefer triggering dbt Cloud jobs via the API from an orchestrator like Airflow, instead of dbt Cloud's own cron schedule?
options: When dbt is one step in a bigger pipeline the orchestrator already manages, rather than the only thing needing scheduling
Never — dbt Cloud jobs can only ever be triggered by cron
Only when there is no Git repository connected
API triggers are purely theoretical and don't actually exist
questions.explain: If dbt is just one step among several that an orchestrator coordinates (e.g., after a raw-data load), an API trigger from that orchestrator is often the cleaner fit.

questions.q: In the real 'Morning Job' example from this lesson, why did the team use separate `dbt run`, `dbt seed`, `dbt run`, `dbt test` steps instead of a single `dbt build`?
options: They wanted seeds loaded in between two separate run steps — more explicit control than dbt build's single dependency-ordered pass gives
dbt build does not exist as a command
Separate steps run tests before any models are built, which dbt build cannot do
There is no reason — both approaches are functionally identical in every case
questions.explain: An explicit step list trades dbt build's simplicity for more control over exactly when each command runs relative to the others.
